# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–11 (Complete – Updated 100)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; winter of second year; spring of third year (auction, financial crisis, engagement rupture); military mobilization period following Napoleon's escape and landing; thaw period with frost-silvered hedges and rain threatening, early light of year; summer of third year; evening with wind off water, salt and tar smell, frost silvering hedges overnight, vespers bells, bees in lavender; early autumn with coughing sickness, dog barking, turnips on cart, river up, price of salt concerns; late April: gusty raw day with rain whipping pavement, end of day with early light, smoke flat over fields; church service with rattling rain on windows; autumn of third year (river crossing at Quenwick); Brighton period following George-Amelia marriage (early spring/late April): turnips on cart, threatening rain, wind off water with salt and tar smell, frost-silvered hedges, flat smoke over fields, ruts and puddles after thaw; Dobbin's delayed arrival bringing news of Belgium orders; early light of year returning; **current: evening after Dobbin's confrontation with John Osborne in City offices; cart loaded with turnips creaking past; wind off water with salt and tar smell; rain predicted but not yet fallen; darkness falling over London; after-dinner period at Russell Square**
- **Primary Locations**: [All previous locations plus] **Brighton** (George-Amelia honeymoon, Rawdon-Rebecca residence, Jos Sedley's visit); Miremere and Quenwick (settlements by Breena Orlwood, Pebin Wexwood); Chatham (embarkation point for Belgium); Belgium (destination of army deployment); **London** (Dobbin's campaign with Osborne family; confrontation with John Osborne in Thames Street counting-house; Russell Square dinner); Cheltenham, Chowringhee, Calcutta (Jos's references); Richmond (omnibus observation point)

## Main Characters

**Captain William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Role in Marriage**: Primary architect of reconciliation between George and Amelia; convinced both to proceed; urged George to act before regiment's orders; presented gold chain and watch to Amelia; groomsman
- **Confrontation with John Osborne - COMPLETED**: Entered City counting-house on Thames Street; received cordial welcome (Mr. Osborne mistakenly believed George was surrendering); revealed regiment will be ordered to Belgium before week's end; urged reconciliation for charity's sake; argued George is "high-minded" and would resist, not submit to, disinheritance threats
- **Osborne's Escalating Reaction**: When Dobbin implied George's true engagement was to Amelia (not a wealthy heiress), Mr. Osborne erupted in fury; recognized Amelia as "swindling old bankrupt's daughter"; accused Dobbin of setting George up; denounced the idea as "fast and loose"; angrily declared George should "buy a broom and sweep a crossing" rather than marry her; felt personally betrayed, declaring "my service to you, CAPTAIN"
- **Departure and Aftermath**: Realizing argument was futile, Dobbin left the counting-house; Mr. Osborne sank back in chair looking "wildly after him"; Mr. Chopper rushed after Dobbin hatless as he departed the court
- **Internal Conflict Intensified**: Deeply troubled by guilt over role in hastening the marriage; tormented belief that his own unendurable suspense over Amelia drove him to crush uncertainty by hastening marriage; feels he is traitor to both father and son; ashamed that Amelia is always first in his thoughts (before father, mother, sisters, duty—at waking and sleeping, all day long)
- **Post-Confrontation Action**: Returned to hotel and sent brief note to Mr. Osborne conveying Belgium deployment information, hoping it might encourage reconciliation; note also sent reminder to Mr. Chopper expecting him at half-past five (dinner engagement)

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Status - MARRIED**: Married Amelia Osborne late April in chapel near Fulham Road without father's consent
- **Honeymoon**: At Brighton with Amelia enjoying "first blushing days"; expressed delight at Dobbin's arrival; received news of Belgium orders
- **Military Orders**: Confirmed—army ordered to Belgium before week's end; regiment will embark from Chatham imminently
- **Father's Complete Rejection - NOW APPARENT**: John Osborne now knows of marriage to Amelia; considers George a fool; sees marriage as catastrophic; locked himself in study after dinner, suggesting "great catastrophe" affecting George is imminent; possesses detailed records of George's entire life (childhood letters, copy-books, drawing-books, tailor's bills, commissions, childhood mementos including locket of George's hair worn by his mother); his rage focuses particularly on John Sedley's name appearing in George's childhood letters

**Miss Jane Osborne** [CHARACTER]
- Learned of George's marriage from Dobbin; felt violently agitated, nearly fainted; gathered composure and defended George; moved by Dobbin's words about Amelia's faithful heart; immediately spread news to Miss Maria and Miss Wirt
- **Response to Marriage**: Not displeased; Amelia rose in her estimation for spirit displayed; capable of generous forgiveness
- **Current Status**: Present at Russell Square dinner; noted George's empty place at table; maintained silence during gloomy dinner with father

**Miss Maria Osborne** [CHARACTER]
- Learned of George's marriage from Jane; not displeased by runaway match
- **Financial Awareness**: After hearing news, began considering financial implications; with Mr. Frederick Bullock calculated George's "folly" might result in disinheritance, potentially making Maria worth thirty thousand pounds more
- **Current Status**: Present at Russell Square dinner; received unusually bland and attentive treatment from Mr. Bullock; maintained silence during gloomy dinner

**Mr. Frederick Bullock** [CHARACTER]
- Junior partner of wealthy firm; man of the world; understands money and its value
- **Financial Calculation**: Realized George's "folly" might result in disinheritance, making Maria worth thirty thousand pounds more than previously hoped
- **Current Status**: Dined at Russell Square; showed amazement at marriage news; rendered "still and quiet" by Mr. Osborne's dark looks; unusually bland and attentive to Miss Maria during dinner; lacked heart to sit alone drinking wine near "terrible old gentleman in the study"; accompanied ladies upstairs on creaking shoes after dinner

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [CHARACTER - MAJOR DEVELOPMENT]
- Wealthy merchant; George's father; savage, determined man; initially believed George was submitting through Dobbin's visit
- **Eruption and Rejection**: Upon learning George married Amelia (not a wealthy heiress), erupted in fury; called George "d---- fool"; denounced Amelia as "swindling old bankrupt's daughter," "beggar's girl out of a gutter"; accused Dobbin of setting George up; threatened George should "buy a broom and sweep a crossing"; accused Amelia of "dangling and ogling after" George; blamed John Sedley for corrupting George
- **Post-Confrontation - CRITICAL ACTIONS TAKEN**: Retreated to study after dinner with family in gloomy state; locked door, preventing servants and family from accessing him; retrieved mahogany escritoire containing all George's documents since childhood (prize copy-books, drawing-books, childhood letters with love to parents and requests for cake, letters mentioning "godpapa Sedley," letters from West Indies, tailor's bills, drafts, commission newspapers, childhood whip, locket containing George's hair worn by his mother); examined these papers, especially those mentioning John Sedley's name, with "curses quivering on livid lips" and "horrid hatred and disappointment" writhng in his heart; household now understands "great catastrophe" affecting George is imminent; papers marked, docketed, tied with red tape, carefully catalogued with dates

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca Rawdon Crawley)** [CHARACTER]
- Secretly married to Captain Rawdon Crawley; living with him at Brighton; still dunned by creditors; relies on Miss Crawley's relenting

**Captain Rawdon Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Secretly married to Rebecca; at Brighton; over head and ears in debt; Jos Sedley recently replenished purse via billiards; awaiting Miss Crawley's relenting

**Other Characters**: Amelia Osborne (married to George, at Brighton, loved by Miss Jane), Miss Crawley (at Brighton, still refusing to relent), Mrs. Bute Crawley (at Brighton as nurse), John Sedley (ruined, cursed by John Osborne), Mrs. Sedley (Amelia's mother), Jos Sedley (at Brighton)

## Critical Facts and Status (Updated)

- **GEORGE-AMELIA MARRIAGE - COMPLETED, HONEYMOON ONGOING, FATHER NOW KNOWS**: Married late April without father's consent; at Brighton; John Osborne now fully aware and in state of rage; locked himself in study after learning truth; examined lifetime of George's papers with murderous thoughts toward Sedley name
- **DOBBIN'S STRATEGIC CAMPAIGN - COMPLETED, PARTIALLY SUCCESSFUL**: Successfully secured support of Miss Jane, Miss Maria, and Miss Wirt before confronting father; news spread immediately with family not displeased (except father); Amelia's estimation rose for spirit displayed; **confrontation with John Osborne unsuccessful**—Osborne rejected all reconciliation arguments; erupted in fury upon learning Amelia's identity
- **MILITARY CRISIS URGENT**: Regiment ordered to Belgium before week's end; soldiers facing "great and certain risk" and possible fatal outcomes; mobilization imminent from Chatham
- **JOHN OSBORNE'S CATASTROPHIC RESPONSE - NOW UNFOLDING**: Knows truth of marriage; locked in study after dinner; rage directed at Sedley connection; possesses complete documentation of George's life; household expects "great catastrophe" affecting George to follow; disinheritance appears likely and imminent
- **FINANCIAL IMPLICATIONS REALIZED**: Mr. Frederick Bullock calculated Maria might inherit thirty thousand pounds more if George disinherited; family understanding matter through financial lens; Mr. Bullock's attentiveness to Maria has increased accordingly
